description: Maps every file of components/dev-skills/skills to the upstream file it was adapted from, at the pinned commit. Checked by scripts/dev-skills-drift.mjs; the CREDITS.md table is generated from it.

adaptations: Renamed `pigpen-tdd`; an opening note names the source and the pin.
Added a paragraph that makes it an explicit test-first mode (load it when asked for TDD, or when an accepted plan selects red-green-refactor).
Reads `CONTEXT.md` as well as `GLOSSARY.md`.
Added the independent-oracle rule to *What a good test is*, and "prefer existing seams, and the highest seam possible" to *Seams*.
Removed the pointers to `tests.md` and `mocking.md` and the paragraph that calls the `codebase-design` Skill: none of them is shipped.
*Rules of the loop*: added the mutation gate, the cover-the-edges rule and the never-bend-a-test rule; the review reference names `pigpen-code-review`.
Renamed `pigpen-diagnosing-bugs`; an opening note names the source and the pin.

Condensed: the phase prose is shortened and the checklists became bullets or prose. The ten-way loop list, *Redact*, minimise, ranked hypotheses, tagged debug logs and the cleanup list keep their content.
Reads `CONTEXT.md` as well as `GLOSSARY.md`, and notes that a surprising behavior may be a decision that was written down.
Loop step 10 drives a human with a small prompting script; the `scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh` of the original is not shipped (both mentions removed).
Phase 5: after the fix passes, revert it and confirm the regression test goes red; added "fix the cause, not the symptom" and "report an out-of-scope defect plainly".
Renamed `pigpen-handoff`; an opening note names the source and the pin. The rest of the frontmatter is the original's.
Added that a handoff is session memory, not a deliverable, and is not committed.
Added the index-not-store paragraph: durable knowledge is referenced, only what exists nowhere else yet goes inline, and anything worth keeping is filed first.
The suggested-skills section names the skills the next agent should load (PiG has no Skill tool) and the ticket to pick up.
Renamed `pigpen-research`; an opening note names the source and the pin.
The description and body no longer require a background agent or a Markdown file in the repository: a background agent is used only when the setup has subagents.
Added claim records (value, source, basis, reasoning), the rules against presenting an inference as stated and against silently merging conflicting claims, and a delegation brief.
Replaced "write a single Markdown file" with an order for where findings go: the reply, the issue or decision record, the project's established place for research notes; never a loose report file.
Renamed `pigpen-grilling`; an opening note names the source and the pin. The description is the original's.
One question at a time instead of a numbered round of the whole frontier: the question that most unblocks the rest is asked, the answer awaited, the frontier recomputed.
Uses a structured-question tool such as `ask_user_question` when one is available; always allows a free-text answer; proposes a concrete criterion rather than an open question.
Facts are looked up in the environment (a sub-agent only if the setup has them); never ask the human for a revision, a path, a retry or a validation fix.

Uses the project glossary's terms (`GLOSSARY.md` or `CONTEXT.md`) and records accepted answers where the project keeps decisions. The `---` rule between questions of the format block is gone with the rounds.
Renamed `pigpen-prototype`; an opening note names the source and the pin.

Rule 6 points at "the ticket the prototype answers" instead of the implementation issue, and adds a decision record for a decision that is hard to reverse and surprising. Everything else is the original's.

Condensed: the *When this is the right shape* list keeps its examples; steps 2 to 5 lose their elaboration. The single shareable HTML file, the portable pure module, the layout (title, state panel, free-play buttons, tabbed walkthroughs) and the anti-patterns are the original's.
Step 1 uses the project glossary's terms; step 3 says an illegal action explains why it is illegal. The pointer to the prototype Skill names `SKILL.md`.
Condensed: the two sub-shapes, the switcher component and the anti-patterns keep the original's content; the process steps are shorter.
Step 2 adds fake data with realistic shapes and awkward lengths and wiring only the interactions the question is about.
Renamed `pigpen-code-review`; an opening note names the source and the pin. The description drops "in parallel sub-agents".
The two axes run as parallel sub-agents when subagents are available, one after the other otherwise.
Added a paragraph that the review follows evidence that the change works and reports its absence instead of running a broad suite.

Removed the requirement for `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` and the pointer to `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`: the spec is fetched through the project's issue tracker. The standards sources also name agent instructions and lint rules.

The smell baseline, the two briefs, the aggregation rules and *Why two axes* are the original's; the aggregation adds that each finding is tied to a file and line and that whether a defect can wait is the user's call.
Renamed `pigpen-commit`; added `license: Apache-2.0` to the frontmatter and an opening note that states the file was changed, as Apache-2.0 section 4(b) requires.
The subject line asks for a polished, highly descriptive message; the body is strongly encouraged rather than optional (what, why, approach, decisions).
No sign-offs unless the project requires them.
